note: TEA's PUBLISHED statewide percent-responding data for Grade 8 Social Studies, joined to item-index.json so every percentage sits next to the standard TEA tested with it. This is the answer to 'which concepts do Texas students actually miss', and it is measured rather than inferred. It was missing from this directory: the first research pass captured item text, keys, standards and rationales but never these reports, so until now every difficulty claim about a standard here was a proxy.
publisher: Texas Education Agency (TEA), Student Assessment Division
whatTeaPublishesHere: Per TEA's own description of these reports: 'These reports show the question number, the reporting category measured by the question, and the percentage of students selecting each possible answer choice for that test question. Use the item analysis summary reports in conjunction with the released test forms.' So the per-option distribution is official, statewide, and covers every item on the form — including the 2023+ items whose TEXT is permanently unpublished.
licensingPosture: These are percentages, item positions, reporting categories and standard labels — facts ABOUT the test, not TEA's expressive content. No item text, stem, option text or rubric language is reproduced in this file. README.md section 4.3 recommendation 3 identifies exactly this category as the safest and still very valuable use, needing no permission. The licensing question in section 4 still governs items/*.json; it is not reopened or resolved here.
howTheJoinIsSelfChecking: A report row is accepted for an item only when BOTH the reporting category and the starred (correct) column agree with the official answer key already recorded in item-index.json from a TEA key document. The reports do not name the subject per row and, in 2022 and 2023, interleave Science and Social Studies in two columns that the PDF text layer flattens — so the key and the reporting category are what distinguish a Social Studies row from a Science row that happens to share an item number. Where that still leaves more than one candidate the item is written to `unresolved` and NOT to `items`.
readingCaveats: Percentages are TEA's published integers and need not sum to 100: they are rounded, and TEA excludes some populations from percent-responding (2018-2022 footnote: 'Students who took the paper STAAR with embedded supports version of the test are not included'; 2023 footnote: 'Results for students who took the test on Paper, Braille or ASL are not included').
percentCorrect is a DIFFICULTY figure for one item, not a mastery figure for a standard. A standard with one item has one measurement, and a hard item and a hard standard are not the same claim.

Partial-credit and non-multiple-choice items are in `partialCredit`, not `items`, because column A means 'full credit' rather than 'option A' for those — see each row's `legend`. Mixing them into a percentCorrect ranking would compare different quantities.

There is no 2020 administration (STAAR was cancelled). 2024 and 2025 statewide item analysis reports were not located at this URL family during this pass and are NOT captured here; absence in this file is not evidence they do not exist.
No aggregate per-standard mean is stored in this file on purpose. A derived table sitting beside its source is how the module deck acquired four hand-copies; recompute it from `items`.
